svg.title: WALDO picks references from a middle band of sliced Wasserstein distance
svg.desc: Two panels. Left: a query image and a healthy reference are each a cloud of patch tokens, shown as blue and orange points in 2-D. Both clouds are projected onto a random direction theta; the projected values are sorted, and the i-th smallest query value is paired with the i-th smallest reference value. The pairing lines have widths proportional to entropy weights, and the weighted sum of squared paired gaps, averaged over many directions, is the sliced Wasserstein distance. Right: a histogram of that distance from one query to every reference in a healthy pool, with a shaded band between the 30th and 70th percentiles. Schematic curves show variance falling and squared bias rising with distance, so the total error is U-shaped with its minimum inside the band, and five blue dots mark references chosen by a determinantal point process, spread across the band.
svg.text: Sliced W₂: project on a random θ, sort, pair in order
weighted SW₂ = (Σ wᵢ (p(i) − q(i))²)¹ᐟ², mean over M θs
line width = entropy weight wᵢ; O(TM log T), not O(T³)
weighted SW₂(query, reference) across the healthy pool
Blue dots: K = 5 DPP picks spread by det(L_S). Curves
are schematic: the paper argues the U, it does not derive it.
WALDO ranks healthy references by patch-level sliced Wasserstein and keeps the middle band
References closer than the 30th percentile look too alike for the VLM to localise differences; farther than the 70th, anatomy
no longer matches. Within the band a quality-gated DPP kernel exp(−β·SW₂(hi, hj)) picks K references that are far from each other.
